solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old dandy gets spun, dancing with former lover

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and change places, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged
leman is an archaic word for a sweetheart or lover

explanation.surface: An elderly fop, twirled round on the dance floor with an ex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' looks like the verb of the sentence but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A puss-gentleman is an old term for an effeminate, foppish man, which is what a dandy was.

clue.text: Foreigner in South Sea island, one long immured in confusion

indicators.note: to be immured is to be walled up inside something

parts.note: pi (or pie) is printers' type jumbled in confusion
a means one
a lag is a convict, one held a long time; long serves as that adjective here

explanation.surface: An outsider on a Pacific island, locked away for years in the chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one long immured' is a long-term prisoner: an old lag sits inside PI.
explanation.definitionFit: Palagi is the Samoan word for a white person or outsider, a foreigner in Samoa in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Magic mark, one left after design lacks study at edges

indicators.note: the word lacks the letters named next, so they are taken away
the removed letters come off the two ends, split between the front and the back

parts.note: taken as written
a den is a study; 'at edges' splits it, DE at the front and N at the back
Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A sorcerer's symbol, its design trimmed so one line remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' is split across both ends of the design, two letters at the front and one at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A sigil is a seal or sign believed to have occult power, a symbol drawn in magic.

clue.text: Small bouquet's ordered up for mainframe maestro?

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending letters up reverses their order

parts.note: a posy is a small bunch of flowers

explanation.surface: Flowers ordered for a computer boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' suggests rearranging, but 'ordered up' reads backwards in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A sysop is a system operator, the person who runs a computer system or bulletin board, hence a computing expert.

clue.text: One's trunks are regularly soaked — draining a pond involves this

indicators.note: the phrase involves, that is contains within it, the answer

parts.note: the run of letters spans three words

explanation.surface: Swimmers' trunks get wet when someone drains a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunks' suggests swimwear, but they are tree trunks standing in flood water.
explanation.definitionFit: A gapó is an area of Amazonian forest flooded each rainy season, so its tree trunks stand in water.

clue.text: Short sleep I have after shooting up anaesthetic drug

indicators.note: in a down light, letters shooting upward read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone dozes after injecting a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting up' reads as drug injection, but it is the signal to reverse the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Evipan is a trade name for hexobarbital, a barbiturate formerly used as a general anaesthetic.

clue.text: What does T stand for? Start to search in web

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for web

parts.note: tela is an anatomical term for a web-like tissue

indicators.note: the start of the next word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of search

explanation.surface: Puzzling over what an initial stands for, so beginning an internet search.
explanation.walkthrough: 'web' suggests the internet; it is a Latin anatomical word.
explanation.definitionFit: T is the SI unit symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density.

clue.text: East German city providing some gear for mountaineers

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East
An old city in western Germany

explanation.surface: A city in eastern Germany supplies kit for climbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like one adjective, but East gives its own letter and the city follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An étrier is a short rope ladder that climbers clip to a piton, an item of climbing equipment.

clue.text: Potential diner making a wry face

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person to be fed
second meaning: a grimace, an old sense of the word

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one person pulling a face at a meal, but 'making' only joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependant who must be fed is called a mouth, and Chambers also gives the noun as a grimace or pout.

clue.text: Incautious Ed M: ~I mind these after mess-up!~

definitions.text: Incautious Ed M: ~I mind these after mess-up!~

indicators.note: a mess-up scrambles things, so the name's letters are jumbled
the answer plus the words named make the jumble, so those words are taken away once it is done

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters come out

explanation.surface: Ed Miliband, then Labour leader, forgot part of a 2014 conference speech and is resolving to use prompters next time.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus I MIND is an anagram of INCAUTIOUS ED M. Ed Miliband famously left out a passage on the deficit when speaking from memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocues are screens that scroll a speech's text for a speaker to read, so a politician need not memorise it.

clue.text: One not born in N. African country entering Israel as immigrant

parts.note: a, the indefinite article, means one

indicators.note: 'not born' asks for the abbreviation for born to be left out of the country's name

parts.note: Libya lies in North Africa
b. is the standard abbreviation for born

explanation.surface: Someone foreign-born moves from North Africa to settle in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not born' reads as the surface's foreign-born idea, but it simply drops the abbreviation for born from the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliya (from Hebrew 'ascent') is the act of Jewish immigration to Israel, so it names the process of arriving there to settle.

clue.text: A fool engaging gardeners, one with no lofty ideas about mankind

definitions.text: one with no lofty ideas about mankind

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit
a mali is a gardener in India

explanation.surface: A foolish employer of gardeners who thinks little of humanity.
explanation.definitionFit: An animalist holds that humans are merely animals, so takes a low, unexalted view of human nature.

clue.text: Battle shifts, rear moving to front

indicators.note: the last letter is taken from the back of the word and placed at its start

parts.note: tours of duty are shifts or spells of work

explanation.surface: A fight moves its rearguard up to the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' reads like the verb of the sentence, but it is a noun meaning spells of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Stour is an old and dialect word for a conflict or tumult, so it is a synonym of battle.

clue.text: A predecessor of Roy H sounded old-fashioned

definitions.note: 'old-fashioned' flags the archaic past participle of ring

wordplay.note: Roy Hodgson managed England; Ron Greenwood held the job before him, shortened to his first name and initial

explanation.surface: An earlier England football manager came across as dated.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy H is Roy Hodgson, England manager in 2015; an earlier one was Ron Greenwood, written RON G.
explanation.definitionFit: Rong is an old form of rung, the past participle of ring, so it means tolled or sounded.

clue.text: Tweaks take shape from right to left — in this? (7, two words)

definitions.text: Tweaks take shape from right to left — in this?

indicators.note: reading from right to left is reading the words backwards

parts.note: to nip is to pinch or tweak
plans gel when they come together and take shape

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler's twisting deliveries curling across the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: NIPS GEL read backwards gives the answer. The whole clue also describes it: a leg-break bowler tweaks the ball so it turns from the right-hander's leg side, moving right to left as the bowler sees it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg spin is wrist spin bowling in cricket, where the bowler twists the ball so it breaks from leg towards off, a sideways turn.

clue.text: What with a bit of panache may get actors up?

definitions.text: What with a bit of panache may get actors up?

indicators.note: the answer's letters plus two more may get, that is become, the phrase that follows once rearranged
the answer is what you have once the added letters that come with it are taken away again

parts.note: taken as written
a bit of panache is its first letter
the letters of these words, rearranged from the answer plus the two extras

explanation.surface: Asking what device, used with flair, lifts performers on to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer with A and P added rearranges to ACTORS UP, so take A and P out of those letters. The whole clue also defines it, since a scruto is a stage trapdoor that raises actors.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruto is a spring trapdoor in a theatre stage through which performers can appear suddenly, so it is what raises actors up.

clue.text: Tropical diver, celebrated bolshy? No end

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to be sung of is to be celebrated in song
bolshy is British slang for uncooperative or rebellious

explanation.surface: A famous, stroppy diver, perhaps a sporting rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: The sungrebe is a tropical American bird, a finfoot that dives and swims among water plants.

clue.text: Exaggerate, close to following wreath laid in grave (8, three words)

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the piece named before it is placed second, at the end
something laid in a hollow is placed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pit is a grave dug in the ground
a lei is a Hawaiian garland or wreath of flowers
on can mean close to or near, as in 'on the coast'

explanation.surface: A funeral scene: a wreath laid on a grave, with a request to overstate things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' places ON after the grave with its wreath.
explanation.definitionFit: To pile it on is an idiom for overstating or laying it on thick, which is to exaggerate.

clue.text: Draught, hot, in ancient abyss

parts.note: a gulp is a swallow, a draught of drink
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A swig of something hot, taken down into the depths.
explanation.definitionFit: Gulph is an obsolete spelling of gulf, a deep chasm, so 'ancient' signals the old form of the word.

clue.text: She'll give a mother a bit of help

definitions.text: She'll give a mother a bit of help

parts.note: taken as written
ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: only a small piece of the next word is used: its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of help

explanation.surface: A description of a nanny who assists a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An amah is a nurse or maidservant in East and South Asia, a woman employed to help a mother with her children.

clue.text: Dipping-needle: I see to mini lunar shifts

indicators.note: things that shift move position, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
see sounds like the letter C
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notices tiny movements of the moon on a compass-like instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' becomes the letter C, a standard crossword conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: An inclinatorium is a dip circle, a magnetic needle that tilts to measure the inclination of the earth's field.

clue.text: Concealed former home of Olivier as it was

parts.note: late means former, as in the late chairman

parts.words: home of Olivier as it was
parts.note: Laurence Olivier was first director of the National Theatre, whose largest auditorium bears his name

explanation.surface: A hidden former residence of the actor Laurence Olivier.
explanation.walkthrough: NT is the National Theatre in London, which Olivier founded as director.
explanation.definitionFit: Latent means present but hidden or not yet developed, close to concealed.

clue.text: Page missing, mad poet's lines for sale (6, two words)

indicators.note: mad means crazy and disordered, so the remaining letters are jumbled
with the page missing, its abbreviation is dropped from the word

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for page
taken as written
ll is the abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: A crazy poet's verses go on sale with a page lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are to sell are on offer, so the phrase means available for sale.

clue.text: ~This alloy's not constant~ – schoolmistress has me enthralled

indicators.note: to be enthralled is to be held captive, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: marm (ma'am) was the address for a schoolmistress
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher who has the speaker spellbound, against a riddle about a metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition calls itself 'this', so it reads as the answer describing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmem is a shape-memory alloy that changes shape with temperature, so its form is not fixed.

clue.text: Drape central feature of gravestone

indicators.note: the central feature is what lies in the middle of the next word

parts.note: the middle letters

explanation.surface: A cloth hung over the centrepiece of a tombstone.
explanation.definitionFit: To vest is to clothe or robe, as a priest is vested, so it can mean drape.

clue.text: Stirs sponge up, to cook inside

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom upward
the second piece is placed inside the first

parts.note: a sponge is a heavy drinker, a sot
to do is to cook, as in done to a turn

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: stir the sponge mixture and bake it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirs' and 'sponge' paint baking, but stirs is a plural noun and the sponge is a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To-dos are fusses or commotions, and stirs are commotions too.

clue.text: Pastry one's consumed in Florence

indicators.note: something consumed is taken inside, so this piece goes within the name

parts.note: Flo is the short form of the name Florence
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Pastry eaten in the Italian city of Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence looks like the Italian city but is a woman's name, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Filo is very thin flaky pastry used in Greek and Middle Eastern cooking such as baklava.

clue.text: Son in book decapitated? We may have to thank Agave for this!

definitions.text: We may have to thank Agave for this!

indicators.note: the son's abbreviation goes inside the other word
removing the head takes off the first letter

parts.note: publishers call each book a title
s is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: In Greek myth Agave beheaded her son Pentheus, so the clue seems to ask who to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: Agave is both the mythical mother and the plant genus that yields the fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a strong fibre obtained from several agave and yucca plants, used for cord and brushes.

clue.text: Shoot not dead on Asian tree, source of astringent resin

indicators.note: 'not dead' tells you to leave out the abbreviation for dead

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant
d. is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
the tea plant is an Asian shrub or small tree

explanation.surface: A shoot, still alive, growing on an Asian tree that yields a resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian tree' wants to be part of the definition; it is the tea plant, and the definition is the last four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Butea is a genus of Asian trees, including the flame of the forest, which yields an astringent gum called Bengal kino.

clue.text: Voice impediment? Ignore initial hush

indicators.note: the opening part of the word is ignored and left off

parts.note: a stutter is a speech impediment
st! is an interjection calling for silence

explanation.surface: A speech defect: someone is told to pay no heed to their first stammer.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice something is to say it, and utter is a verb meaning to say out loud.

clue.text: King in awaiting first shot maybe hid in oak?

definitions.text: King in awaiting first shot maybe hid in oak?

indicators.note: the king's abbreviation is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a golfer who has teed up is ready to play the opening shot
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king expecting gunfire hides in an oak tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: after the battle of Worcester, Charles II hid in an oak tree from Parliament's soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Treed means driven up a tree and trapped there, as a hunted animal or a fugitive king might be.

clue.text: In love, I deliberate being taken back — I don't expect a response

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed inside the word for love

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love, and the word means love
taken as written: the first I in the clue, not the one in the closing words

indicators.note: taking something back returns it the way it came, so these letters run in the opposite order

parts.note: a set purpose is a deliberate one

explanation.surface: A lover wavering, then expecting no reply.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the voice of the thing defined: a rhetorical question says it needs no answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotesis is the rhetorical question, a figure of speech asked for effect with no reply expected.

clue.text: Fire in home of tarts, well off

indicators.note: taking something off removes it, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: Bakewell is a Derbyshire town famous for its Bakewell tart
taken as written; these letters come out

explanation.surface: A blaze in a brothel, but everyone got out unharmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tarts' suggests prostitutes, but they are the pastries named after a town in Derbyshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire pottery is to bake it hard in a kiln, so bake is a synonym of fire.

clue.text: Study in group taking exam?

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a set is a group
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: Revising alongside others before an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is an example: exam candidates sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedent is a rare word for seated, and someone sitting an exam is seated at a desk.

clue.text: What blows east, mer ruffled? Sailors will understand it (7, two words)

definitions.text: What blows east, mer ruffled? Sailors will understand it

indicators.note: ruffled water is disturbed, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: mer is French for sea; the letters are taken as written

explanation.surface: A wind blowing from the east over a choppy sea, described in jargon only sailors follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: words like 'blows' and directions such as 'east' are nautical vocabulary a sailor grasps.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea term is a nautical expression, the jargon that seafarers use and know.

clue.text: In quality slice of beef — you may find this

definitions.text: In quality slice of beef — you may find this

indicators.note: the selected letter is put inside the word for quality

parts.note: tone is a quality, as of sound or colour

indicators.note: a slice is just a thin piece, here the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the first letter of beef

explanation.surface: A cut of good-quality beef that contains a particular bone.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a T-bone steak is a quality cut of beef, and this bone is found in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bone is a steak cut from the sirloin containing a T-shaped bone, a prime cut of beef.

clue.text: Lake: everyone's got on board this large tub

indicators.note: what is on board is carried within, so the answer is held inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Everyone climbs aboard a big tub out on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeve (or kieve) is a large tub or vat, used for brewing or bleaching.

clue.text: Will belters seldom need to be rewritten for this?

definitions.text: Will belters seldom need to be rewritten for this?

indicators.note: rewriting reorders the material, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a blockbuster novel ever needs revising to reach the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a belter is a hit, and hit books seldom need rewriting to reach top-seller status.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestsellerdom is the status or world of bestselling books, the commercial success that a smash-hit title achieves.
